title: Candidate handoff & shadowing checklist — Aug 2025
content:
Overview:
This doc captures interview debrief takeaways, the candidate handoff items for hiring manager and onboarding buddy, and a practical shadowing/checklist plan to accelerate ramp. Intended audience: Eng hiring panel, hiring manager (Marco), onboarding buddy (Aisha), and platform team for infra access.

Recent interview debriefs (summary notes):
- Candidate: Dana Li (backend infra candidate) — onsite loop 2025-07-30. Panel: Marco (hiring mgr), Aisha (team buddy), Liam (serving-runtime), Sofia (SRE).
- Strengths: strong systems reasoning, clear KV cache explanation, pragmatic tradeoffs on batching vs latency. Gave a concrete plan for degraded fallback policy.
- Risks: limited exposure to our internal infra (K8s multi-tenant GPU pools); slower with Python async patterns in prod code.
- Cultural fit: high collaboration signals, asked about postmortems and runbook ownership.

Debrief rubric (quick):
- Technical (scale/design): 8/10 — architecture tradeoffs solid.
- Code/style (pair): 6/10 — passable, can tighten typing and async patterns.
- System ownership/ops: 5/10 — ramp required.
- Hire recommendation: strong hire if we can invest 2-3 week bootcamp and pairing.

Candidate handoff checklist (what hiring manager must confirm):
- [ ] Finalize compensation range and draft offer (owner: Marco) — target send by 2025-08-06 (JIRA: ENG-1203).
- [ ] Confirm start date availability and visa paperwork (owner: Marco).
- [ ] Assign onboarding buddy and prepare initial schedule (owner: Aisha).
- [ ] Grant provisional dev infra access tokens and test cluster namespace (owner: infra-team). Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-987.

Onboarding buddy plan (Aisha): first 2 weeks detailed schedule:
Week 0 (pre-start):
- Share pre-read: Onboarding Runbook page, team architecture diagram, CI quickstart.
- Ensure laptop image and credentials provisioned; checklist link: confluence:Onboarding-Runbook-2025#prework

Week 1 (focus: context & local dev):
- Day 1: Introductions, Slack channels, calendar blocks, 1:1 with hiring manager.
- Day 2: Local dev environment pairing (30m), run the demo app, open first tiny PR.
- Day 3-5: Shadow on-call rotation and watch a live rollout (pair with Sofia).

Week 2 (focus: code & infra):
- Pair sessions on: KV cache hotpath, batching config, and quantization test harness.
- Small ownership task: fix a flaky integration test and ship a CI fix.

Shadowing schedule (concrete slots):
- Mon 09:30-11:00 — Pair on local dev + run through demo (Aisha).
- Wed 14:00-15:30 — Observe on-call paging and postmortem rubric (Sofia).
- Thu 10:00-11:30 — Deep dive on serving-runtime batching (Liam).
- Fri 16:00 — Sync with product on rollout expectations (Marco).

Interview follow-ups and tasks (immediate):
- Marco: prepare offer draft + comp numbers by 2025-08-06.
- Aisha: create a dedicated onboarding channel and pin the 2-week schedule (by 2025-08-04).
- Liam: add code pointers and a short 'starter' PR template in repo README (by 2025-08-07).
- Sofia/Infra: provision namespace and a GPU slot for a smoke test (ticket INFRA-987).

Open questions / blockers:
- Access: should we give Dana production-read only access on day 3 or restrict to staging until end of probation? (Action: Marco to decide).
- Training content: we lack a short internal module on GPU memory debugging — who owns this? (Suggestion: Liam to draft).
- Pair bandwidth: several pairing slots conflict with release freeze next week; consider remote async sessions for first week.

Notes to self / rough items (informal):
- Quick wins to show candidate early: reproduce a small perf regression dashboard and walk through the tracing.
- Slack refs: #eng-onboard (pinned: onboarding checklist), thread: slack.com/archives/C0234XYZ/p165...
- Confluence templates used: Onboarding-Runbook-2025, New-Hire-90-Day-Plan.

Post-hire ramp metrics (how we will evaluate success first 90 days):
- Week 2: able to run local integration tests and open a PR.
- Week 6: lead a small ops change and own rollout.
- Week 12: independently respond to an on-call page and run a blameless postmortem.

Quick retrospective on the interview loop (meta):
- Panel had inconsistent rubric language — standardize the 'ops' criteria for infra hires.
- Add a pairing exercise that includes a short async Python task (to test async patterns).

End — comments welcome. If you want edits, flag inline with initials (e.g., "MP: prefer shorter shadowing sessions").
